reasons: The author's MARKET_VOLUME disagreement is supported: the 192 sales a month are split across 40 sellers, and Brain's reading treats all of them as available to one new listing. CONDITIONAL with a live pace test is the right stance, and the arithmetic holds (39 x $29 = $1,131; less $117 in fees leaves $1,014; the last payout settles on day 29). But the validation is not a complete decision rule. Proof and continue need 12 or more sales by day 10 and stop needs fewer than 5, so a result of 5 to 11 sales has no instruction. At 5-11 sales by day 10 the listing cannot reach 39 by day 27 at that pace, and the plan does not say what to do.
findings: Validation gap: 5-11 sales by day 10 falls between stop (<5) and continue (>=12) and has no rule. Either make the stop threshold <12, or define what a partial pace means: a revised target, or adding openings.
Tight window: 27 sales need to land by day 26 so that they settle by day 29. There is no slack in the plan if payouts slip.
The plan does not say how the 60 paid pre-orders already on this offer's page relate to the listing's sales: whether they are in hand, whether they count toward the 39, and when they settle.
